title: Full Gimli AE's 128-Bit Security Claim
summary: The paper reports attacks only on reduced-round Gimli, leaving the full AE scheme's claimed security relative to its key length unexplained.

formal_statement.body: Explain or match the $2^{128}$-security claim for full Gimli AE despite its $256$-bit key.

scope.domain: Symmetric cryptanalysis of the full Gimli authenticated-encryption scheme.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Explain or match the full Gimli AE scheme's 128-bit security claim despite its 256-bit key; the reported attacks apply only to reduced-round variants.

citations.label: Automatic Verification of Differential Characteristics: Application to Reduced Gimli

progress.summary: The source explicitly asks why the AE scheme claims 128-bit security while using a 256-bit key. Its reported state-recovery attacks concern only reduced 5- and 9-round variants and do not threaten full Gimli.
citation_labels: Fukang Liu et al., Automatic Verification of Differential Characteristics: Application to Reduced Gimli
